questions: Will the user explicitly waive the current mechanical provider-routing gaps after reviewing this evidence, or require the registry bug to be fixed out of band before design approval?
assumptions: The plugin remains local and file-backed under reusable_internal posture; it does not become a remote policy or deployment service.
Canonical state continues to be architecture.json, design.json, and map.json, with Markdown and events treated as non-authoritative views/evidence.
findings: Existing stableHash, atomic rename, file-lock, and expected-hash mechanisms provide the correct primitives for posture integrity, but the new posture and provenance references must use them consistently across every canonical boundary.

Current migration is preview-by-default and explicit-apply, but v2.1 needs a stated recovery source and field-preservation verification because atomic replacement prevents partial writes but does not by itself reverse a semantically bad migration.

The MCP surface receives plan/project roots only at process startup and does not execute provider commands, which limits runtime injection; posture changes must preserve this non-executing validation boundary.
Provider evidence deliberately preserves raw output, so credential-like content and machine-specific absolute paths require validation or rejection before persistence rather than silent copying.

Resolving symlink-installed skill roots is necessary, but discovery should resolve only explicitly configured roots, deduplicate real paths, and avoid recursive traversal through arbitrary symlink entries.
The largest scope risk is not missing production hardening but allowing provider suggestions or compact reconstruction to add behaviors above the selected profile ceiling.

risks.description: A stale or partially validated posture/provenance reference makes canonical plan state internally inconsistent.
risks.mitigation: Use canonical hashing, file locks, atomic replacement, expected-hash writes, target existence checks, and negative tests for dangling/stale refs.

risks.description: A syntactically valid v2.1 migration loses legacy topology, evidence, decisions, or artifact links.
risks.mitigation: Keep preview as default, require explicit apply, retain a declared recovery source, compare preservation manifests, and run round-trip/strict validation before completion.

risks.description: Raw provider output persists credentials, tokens, or machine-specific absolute paths into portable plan artifacts.
risks.mitigation: Validate provider evidence before persistence, reject credential-like values, reject machine absolute paths, and cover both with portability/security fixtures.

risks.description: The provider-discovery symlink fix traverses outside configured roots or enters a cycle.
risks.mitigation: Resolve and deduplicate explicitly configured root paths only; do not recursively follow arbitrary symlink entries; test cycles and outside-root entries.

risks.description: A task override or profile transition lowers mandatory safety floors and admits silent invalidity, destructive loss, credential exposure, or runaway cost.
risks.mitigation: Make safety floors non-overridable; require explicit promotion/design re-entry for broader posture changes; reject conflicting refs before leaf planning or execution.

risks.description: Provider recommendations or post-compact reconstruction silently expand work above the approved behavior budget.
risks.mitigation: Carry exact posture hashes and exclusions, require provenance for executable behavior, preserve over-ceiling suggestions only as deferred candidates, and perform subtractive finalization first.

risks.description: Concurrent writers overwrite an approved posture, design revision, or architecture default without detecting the lost update.
risks.mitigation: Reuse file locks and expected-hash compare-and-swap behavior for every canonical mutation and test conflict failures.

findings: The upstream engineering directory is a family of composable skills, not one mandatory phase sequence.
grill-with-docs is a thin user-invoked orchestration entry that delegates interviewing and domain-modeling behavior instead of reimplementing them.
Its durable outputs are intentionally narrow: resolved terminology may enter CONTEXT.md, only hard-to-reverse surprising tradeoffs merit ADRs, and other decisions can remain conversation-only.
codebase-design supplies module, interface, seam, depth, locality, adapter, deletion-test, and test-surface heuristics, but it is a reference discipline without its own stopping rule.
wayfinder treats a multi-session map as a low-resolution index over detailed decision tickets, with explicit frontier, fog, blockers, and out-of-scope state.
These mechanisms favor composition contracts and verified handoffs over copying mature provider logic into the planning plugin.

Add only a versioned input/output and persistence adapter when the mature skill's workflow is suitable but its envelope differs.
Reimplement only when a documented compatibility, portability, licensing, availability, or required-behavior gap prevents composition.

risks: Copying mature skill logic creates duplicate workflow ownership and upstream drift.

requirements: R-POSTURE: Model spike, experiment, reusable_internal, and production as intent profiles rather than a quality ladder.
R-PERSIST: Carry a hash-bound posture through project defaults, maps, nodes, designs, handoffs, and compact-safe execution context.
R-PROVENANCE: Admit executable work only when it traces to an approved requirement/design/contract, an observed failure, or a mandatory safety floor.
R-BUDGET: Bind implementation to approved observable behavior and the minimum code needed to satisfy it.
R-EXPERIMENT: Require hypothesis, measurement validity, reproducibility, and fail-loud behavior without speculative production capabilities.
R-PROMOTION: Make posture promotion an explicit user-approved change that re-enters design and architecture synchronization.
R-COMPAT: Preserve readable legacy artifacts and require explicit migration before new posture claims are authoritative.
R-APPROVAL-UX: Every human gate renders a bounded inline ApprovalBrief in the active conversation; artifact paths are optional audit references, never the approval interface.

R-COMPOSE: Prefer an installed mature skill through a verified CompositionContract; add a thin adapter only for envelope mismatch, and reimplement only with documented evidence and approved scope provenance.

options.summary: Add a hash-bound EngineeringPosture and scope provenance to the existing architecture, design, map, and handoff states, with explicit v2.1 migration.
tradeoffs: Preserves three canonical states and survives compact.
Requires compatibility readers, migration, and posture-aware completion checks.

options.summary: Create posture.json as a fourth canonical state shared by architecture, designs, and maps.
tradeoffs: Adds identity, locking, invalidation, and synchronization complexity that exceeds the current need.

options.summary: Express experiment and production modes only in SKILL.md and project constitution prose.
tradeoffs: Cannot reliably enforce scope ceilings, provenance, promotion, or compact-safe references.

selected_option.rationale: It combines Spec Kit-style durable policy and OpenSpec-style bounded changes with Superpowers-style behavior-minimal implementation, without creating another canonical database.

invariants: Intent profiles are different definitions of done, not an ordered quality ladder.
Production posture is never inferred from hypothetical future reuse.
No executable node or implemented behavior exists without approved scope provenance.
Spike and experiment work retain mandatory safety floors for silent invalidity, destructive loss, credentials, and runaway cost.
Evidence may propose promotion but cannot apply it; promotion requires explicit user approval and re-enters design.
architecture.json, design.json, and map.json remain the only canonical project/design/map states.
Compact and provider boundaries re-read and verify posture_hash instead of reconstructing posture from prose.
A module or task override cannot weaken the mandatory safety floor; broader posture changes require explicit promotion and design re-entry.
Every ScopeProvenance ref must resolve to a current, hash-verified approved source, observed failure event, or named safety-floor rule before its behavior is executable.
Provider discovery may resolve explicitly configured root symlinks but must not recursively traverse arbitrary symlink entries or persist resolved machine paths.
Provider evidence is persisted only after credential-like values and machine-specific absolute paths are rejected.
A human approval request must be self-contained in the active conversation and must not require opening a file; links are supplementary audit evidence only.
An ApprovalBrief is valid only for the exact current hash; any canonical change invalidates the displayed brief and requires regeneration before approval.

A composed provider retains ownership of its workflow; adaptive-writing-plans constrains inputs, posture, provenance, persistence verification, and handoff normalization but does not duplicate hidden provider logic.
Provider availability, dependencies, invocation, and persisted outputs are independently observable states; discovery or plausible prose cannot be treated as successful execution.
Provider installation or upgrade is never automatic, and a reimplementation requires an explicit evidence-backed decision naming why direct composition or a thin adapter is insufficient.
failure_modes: A missing or stale posture reference blocks new posture claims and execution until explicit assessment or migration.
A capability without provenance is rejected from the executable DAG and retained only as a deferred candidate.
A provider recommendation outside the maturity ceiling cannot mutate canonical state or silently expand a leaf plan.
An experiment touching a stable public boundary still triggers the existing design and architecture delta gates for that boundary.
A conflicting module default and task override requires an explicit, hash-bound override decision.
Provider catalog fallback failures remain visible and block claimed provider coverage rather than being treated as no installed provider.
A stale concurrent writer fails its expected-hash check instead of overwriting posture, design, map, or architecture state.
A migration validation failure leaves the original canonical bytes authoritative; a semantic preservation mismatch blocks completion and uses the declared recovery source.
Provider evidence containing credential-like material or machine-specific absolute paths is rejected before raw evidence is stored.
Displaying only an artifact path, an unbounded document dump, or a stale summary is an invalid human-gate handoff and cannot produce approval evidence.

A missing provider dependency, unverified artifact write, version/digest mismatch, or provider execution failure remains visible and cannot silently fall back to a claim of equivalent mature-skill behavior.
Duplicating an upstream workflow without a documented composition blocker creates split ownership and is rejected as unsupported scope.
operational_model: All enforcement remains local and file-backed through schemas, CLI, MCP, and deterministic validators.
This plugin change itself uses reusable_internal posture: stable compatibility and integration tests are required, while telemetry, remote policy, HA, and deployment automation are excluded.
Plan finalization performs a subtractive scope/provenance review before adding missing implementation or validation steps.
Canonical posture mutations reuse file locks, atomic replacement, and optimistic expected-hash checks; assess/check remain read-only and promote remains proposal-only until approval.

Design, architecture, promotion, and waiver gates expose a concise structured ApprovalBrief through CLI/MCP/overview, while the orchestrator renders it inline and asks one explicit confirmation question.

Provider routing uses a composition-first order: direct invocation when the contract matches, a thin versioned adapter for envelope differences, a bounded builtin fallback for unrelated/non-critical work, and evidence-backed reimplementation only after explicit approval.

Interactive grilling/domain providers are conditional Design Gate branches for unresolved terminology or responsibility; module-design references are posture-bounded and cannot impose reusable/production depth requirements on a spike or experiment.

invariants: N-000 is a real control node for map routes, appears once per map, and never substitutes for intent or design approval.
Direct and standalone plan routes emit a Flow Receipt without fabricating a map.
Plan Mode reports pending persistence; it never implies that conversation decisions have already changed repository artifacts.
map.json, design.json, and project architecture.json remain the only canonical map, design, and architecture states; Markdown files are generated views.
Root Design fixes module responsibilities, dependency direction, contract envelopes, posture, and critical scenarios without pre-designing private implementation structure.
Every leaf receives a DesignAssessment, but an independent DesignThread exists only for material contract, dependency, failure, or tradeoff decisions.
A subject has at most one active thread per plan purpose; revision history stays inline in design.json.
A producer may implement an approved candidate contract; a consumer requiring a critical contract waits for verified evidence.
Private contract-preserving implementation choices are autonomous; observable contract, data, migration, failure, security, performance, scope, or posture changes re-enter design.
Contract changes invalidate only exact consumers and their work descendants unless evidence proves that a parent envelope also changed.
Architecture memory belongs to the project and changes only through approved deltas; diff checks guarantee freshness without automatic semantic inference.
Intent profiles are different definitions of done, and production posture is never inferred from hypothetical reuse.
Experiments keep mandatory safety floors for silent invalidity, destructive loss, credentials, and runaway cost while rejecting speculative production hardening.
Provider discovery, dependency readiness, invocation, and persistence verification are separate observable states.
All human approvals are shown inline and bind the exact content hash; file paths are supplementary evidence only.
Provider raw output is stored once and referenced; full conversation transcripts are never persisted as design state.
failure_modes: A missing, duplicated, mutable, or invalid N-000 blocks every work node while leaving design and intent statuses unchanged.
An MCP plan-root mismatch is reported explicitly and uses the bounded repository CLI fallback rather than accepting arbitrary runtime paths.
A child thread is not created for a helper, directory split, or hypothetical seam without an independent contract and verification surface.
A failed critical contract blocks consumers and creates a successor design revision; it cannot be converted into a silent fallback.
A stale thread write fails its expected thread-state hash; changes to independent threads merge only after reloading under the document lock.
A provider recommendation outside the behavior budget remains a deferred candidate and cannot become a map node automatically.
A compact or resume operation with missing exact refs blocks instead of reconstructing posture or design depth from prose.
A syntactically valid migration that loses topology, history, evidence, artifact links, or legacy bytes fails preservation validation and retains its recovery source.
operational_model: The workflow prints a Flow Receipt at intake, status, handoff, resume, and final map reports.
For the current plan, N-000 reconciliation is the first mutation and source edits remain blocked until Root Design approval and a finalised N-001 leaf plan.
DESIGN.md is a generated design graph and index; designs/root.md and material module/relation/task views show current thread revisions.
Module graphs and task DAGs remain separate; strongly connected module groups use a bounded relation design or tracer while the Work DAG remains acyclic.
The first implementation wave validates one narrow end-to-end tracer before broadening module work.
Finalisation performs a subtractive posture and provenance review before adding completeness work.
Composition order is direct provider, thin adapter, bounded fallback, then evidence-backed approved rewrite.

This plugin uses reusable_internal posture: stable local contracts, migration, compatibility, and integration tests are required; remote policy, telemetry, HA, and deployment automation remain excluded.
migration: Read v1 and v2.0 artifacts without inventing N-000, posture, thread parents, or design approval.
Migration preview partitions legacy design revisions by root or node subject, preserves legacy hashes as provenance, and blocks ambiguous parent links.
Explicit apply creates N-000, rewrites map design refs to thread/content refs, writes generated views, and preserves a recovery copy of the exact prior bytes.
Strict schema, hash, DAG, artifact, history, and preservation-manifest validation must succeed before migrated state becomes authoritative.
Plugin refresh preserves the 0.2.0 base version and replaces only the Codex cachebuster suffix.
